newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money up on weekend cover.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money up on weekend cover.

text.p: * Volume rises to 19.581 bln from 8.938 bln pesos
Manila overnight money nudged up to an average of 10.5625 percent on Monday from 10.53125 amid the covering of weekend positions, traders said.
Rates were wedged from 10.625 to 10.5625 percent, with 34 lenders and 21 borrowers.
"We expect rates to remain sideways," a foreign bank dealer said, adding that there was no major development to affect peso liquidity.
In the secondary market for T-bills, buying interest was on short-term bills, dealers said.
"They're quick to dispose in case interest rates rise," a trader said.
Banks are of the view that interest rates have reached bottom and will trend up due to the hike in wages and oil prices brought about by the deregulation of the petroleum industry last February 8.
According to a Reuter poll of seven institutions, banks gave bids ranging from 10.65 to 10.75 for the three-months bills.
